hints.hint_text: Try entering special characters in the login form. What happens with quotes?
SQL comments can help bypass authentication. Try using -- or #
Use: admin' OR '1'='1 as the username
The search results are displayed without sanitization. Can you inject HTML?
Try using <script> tags in your search query
Search for: <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>
Notice the user ID in the URL. What if you change it?
Try accessing /challenge/profile?id=1
The admin user has ID 1. Access their profile directly.
The ping command is executed directly. Can you chain commands?
Use && or ; to execute multiple commands
Try: 127.0.0.1 && type flag.txt (Windows) or 127.0.0.1 && cat flag.txt (Linux)
Inspect your cookies. There's a JWT token. Can you decode it?
JWT tokens have 3 parts. The header specifies the algorithm. What if it's 'none'?
Create a token with alg:none and role:admin, then replace your cookie
The calculator uses eval(). This is extremely dangerous.
You can access Node.js globals like 'process' or 'require'
Try: process.mainModule.require('fs').readFileSync('flag.txt','utf8')
The settings form doesn't validate the request origin. Can you forge a request?
Create an HTML form that submits to /challenge/csrf/update
Use a form with method=POST and auto-submit it from another page
The upload doesn't check file types. What can you upload?
Try uploading a .txt file and see where it's stored
Upload any file, then access /uploads/ to see the directory listing
XML External Entities can read local files. Research XXE attacks.
Define an entity that reads a file: <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM 'file:///flag.txt'>
Submit XML with: <?xml version='1.0'?><!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM 'file:///flag.txt'>]><data>&xxe;</data>
The URL fetcher makes requests on behalf of the server. Can you access internal resources?
Try accessing localhost or 127.0.0.1
Fetch: http://localhost:3000/internal/flag
